thread:
maya: Heads-up — competitor shipped a lightweight fallback that auto-routes to smaller models when latency spikes. Acme pilot just flagged it as a must-have. Do we push a scoped fast-fallback in next sprint or tighten our positioning with a different play?
alex: seeing the signal. quick Q: are we talking auto-routing + model variant fallback, or just region-level downgrade?
cj: technically the fast part is prefix-caching + instant variant switch. can prototype in ~2w if we cut some QA and e2e tests.
sophia: Acme will churn unless we show something. they want a demo by mid-next-week. :grimacing:
liam: from evals the smaller variant loses ~6% quality on long prompts, but latency improves 3-4x for tail requests.
maya: tradeoff noted. Launch criteria suggestion: (1) end-to-end demo for Acme, (2) telemetry hooks for per-tenant downgrade rate, (3) rollback path to avoid quality regressions. Thoughts?
cj: sounds realistic. we should also include a per-route guardrail: only downgrade when predicted latency > 300ms AND prompt length < 1k tokens.
alex: agree on guardrail. ops asks for a circuit-breaker threshold and a metric we can alert on: "downgrade_quality_delta_p90"
liam: add a short eval set from Acme's pilot corpus to measure the real-world delta; otherwise 6% is just lab.
sophia: i'll get them to sign off on a short prompt set today. they want fallback for failures and tail-latency, not for general traffic.
maya: okay plan then: 2-week spike to deliver prototype + demo, integrate Acme eval set, basic telemetry with alerting. if prototype looks noisy, we hold and write a tighter product story.
cj: dev plan: day1 infra + feature flags; day4 model-routing; day7 caching; day10 demo+telemetry hook; day14 cleanup/tests. can we deprioritize one other task?
alex: we can shift the quantization-config task out of next sprint — lower customer impact ATM.
sophia: Acme ok with a minimum viable demo as long as it's clear it's pilot-only. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: PROD deploy scheduled: none — feature flagged rollout only.
maya: two decision axes: parity fast-fallback vs differentiated quality-first fallback. I prefer parity for pilot capture but add a parallel quality-metric improvement backlog item. anyone strongly against?
liam: fine for pilot capture as long as telemetry is locked and we can auto-reverse within 1 hour.
cj: codewise we need feature flag + rollout by tenant; I'll add an emergency rollback endpoint.
alex: update RFC doc with the guardrail thresholds and schedule — i'll own the rollout checklist.
maya: cool. final ask — owners: maya (product), cj (eng), alex (release), sophia (customer signoff), liam (evals). I'll post a short PRD and attach the Acme prompt set once they share.
sophia: pinging Acme now, will confirm prompt set share.
maya: thanks — we'll sync tomorrow 10am to review demo readiness. :rocket:
